allowedAuthoring: Hashing inputs and already built application bytes
Ordinary tests on their existing development fixtures
prohibitedBeforeExecutableSeal: Any model call with this family
sequence: Task 128 driver development on ordinary permit inputs
Separate semantic seal and ten bounded attempts only if all resource prerequisites pass

lanes.resource: Unmodified built daemon entry for cold start, indexing, analysis, preparation and existing history; composition-equivalent launcher with only TextRuntime replaced for controlled answer execution. Real HTTP server and built browser in both. No application method wrappers, exposed GC or profiler in timed samples.
lanes.accounting: One declared diagnostic pass after resource samples. Forward actual OperationBudget charge/check/close calls without changing arguments, return values, caps or scheduling. Report actual accepted/rejected units and budget identities; never infer aggregate work from the largest single budget. No timing/memory qualification from this lane.
lanes.fault: Declared control of owned runtime promises, held HTTP responses and isolated catalog corruption/failure. Record each intervention and use the real admission/validator/recovery. Fault timing is not an uninstrumented resource pass.
lanes.semantic: Actual production daemon and CodexTextRuntime; no model double, altered producer or injected oracle. Ten attempts, one per frozen question, only after separate runtime/account seal.

resourceCases.required: Twenty registered source roots, 240 indexed files, completed compatible analysis, exact S01 original support and native path through the real review route; zero provider calls.

Twenty roots, exactly 10000 indexed files, complete compatible inventory of every eligible code file, useful S01 native review. A budget refusal or unavailable item is a failed positive case, never a pass by bounded refusal.

Three sequential Find-review-admit-publish-history lifetimes per catalog, fixed before observation; exact reviewed prompt/schema and original-only citations, one controlled dispatch each. Report first and every later result, never best-of-three.

Fresh catalog: create 64 actual prepared attempts with nonempty native witnesses through normal HTTP admission, completing each with the controlled runtime. Measure every creation and list request at 1, 20 and 64 rows. The 65th new request must refuse before dispatch and keep current Ready usable; matching old request still replays exactly. No direct SQL seeding of normal capacity rows.

At 20 and 64 retained attempts, keep the real page visible for 30 seconds each, with one Ready preview and one opened saved answer. Record all requests, every response, daemon CPU/memory, browser process tree, main-thread tasks, paint/update lag and pending requests. Do not hide the twenty-row list cost.

A separately owned Ready snapshot expires after its actual ten-minute monotonic lifetime while the browser polls. No fake clock, TTL refresh or generation; display clears by two poll intervals after expiry.

Cancel during preparation, cancel after admission with controlled late provider output, and shutdown during a held worker. Owned work drains, no result publishes, known late usage survives, no second dispatch. Record actual timing separately from deliberately held duration.

Drop the actual admission response after commit, retry the same request from the browser, and prove one durable attempt/dispatch. Change question while a review response is held; its late arrival must not restore old content.

Reopen stopped full catalogs at 20 and 64 attempts through the real entry point. History bytes and authorized originals remain exact, transient IDs disappear, an interrupted active attempt never dispatches itself, and same-ID replay returns persisted input.

Publish enough actual analyses to evict the inventory used by Ready, without replacing its source build. Exact held witness still admits; saved authorized history survives further eviction and restart. No current inventory substitution.

Isolated retained catalog copies: change engineer review, source policy and published build at each of the three real validation boundaries. Reject dispatch/publication at the appropriate boundary, retain usage, and hide late browser context. Also replace review/source scope during saved-history fetch.

Revoke t-boundary-notes at 64 prepared rows. All dependent text and witnesses purge, original/source access fences, tombstones still count toward 64, and the browser shows no late context. Separately inject one declared purge failure, retain pending state, then prove real startup recovery without dispatch.

In an isolated catalog copy remove or corrupt an original required by an existing witness. Revalidation refuses without substituting native IDs, current inventory or legacy input. Also observe naturally incomplete lexical support if present; never inject an oracle passage into retrieval to rescue a case.

Exactly one model-free preparation for each S01-S10 case in its declared variant/setup. Verify required original tuples, native-required/omission outcomes and note provenance before model eligibility. Missing support is a failed prerequisite, not an unanswerable-model credit.

One diagnostic pass for S01 at each size, complete prepared worker, and answer-list requests at 20/64 actual witnesses. Sum all actual budget charges by enclosing HTTP/worker lifetime. Compare outputs with the resource lane after only UUID/time/path normalization; preserve raw bytes. Missing accounting or a mismatch fails qualification.

thresholds.units: Bytes are UTF-8 or actual process/storage bytes as named; MiB is 1048576 bytes. Durations use monotonic clocks; limits are maxima, not percentiles.

semanticBudget.unknownUsage: Stop before another attempt; record the missing usage and incomplete gate. This is a sequential stop threshold, not a guaranteed provider-side token or monetary cap.
semanticBudget.preflight: Bind canonical personal executable/configHome/profile, launcher and binary hashes, qualified CLI version, policy, requested model, safe configuration fingerprint and runtime-reported identity before case one. No credentials or authentication stores in artifacts. Incompatible policy/version is a stop, not permission to update the frozen run.
semanticBudget.transportOrSemanticFailure: No repeat. Preserve the failed case; continue remaining cases only within all frozen budgets and unchanged identity/scope. An authorization, integrity, accounting or tooling violation stops the run immediately.

stopRules: Append a started record and fsync before the first candidate read; that consumes the family for this predeclared sequence even on setup or harness failure.

A failed required positive, threshold or assertion makes the gate fail. Independent remaining resource cases may be recorded once unless integrity, scope, watchdog or capacity threatens evidence retention.

Any resource failure blocks semantic execution and exhausts its reserved continuation. No repaired rerun, resized limit, warmed-only substitution, renamed case or omitted failed sample can pass this family.
One process-tree watchdog owns only this run's children; preserve raw outputs and stopped catalogs on every exit. A storage ceiling stops new work; do not delete earlier evidence to continue.
Ordinary permit development can repeat; all previously exhausted resource/model families remain exhausted.
